\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{amssymb}

\title{Lecture 7: Robust Estimation}
\author{Compiled from the spring seminar notes}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Setup}
Let $X_1, \dots, X_n$ be independent draws from a
contamination model $F = (1 - \varepsilon) G + \varepsilon H$,
where $G$ is the nominal distribution and $H$ is arbitrary.
The contamination proportion $\varepsilon$ is unknown, and we
assume throughout that $\varepsilon \in (0, 1/2)$ so that the
nominal component remains identifiable. Choosing $\varepsilon$
adaptively is impossible without further structure, so the
estimators below are calibrated to the worst case over $H$.
The breakdown point is the largest $\varepsilon$ for which the
estimator remains bounded in probability.
We write $\bar{x}$ for the sample mean and
$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} (x_i - \bar{x})^2$ for the
empirical variance. Under the nominal model,
$\mathbb{E}[X^4] < \infty$ is enough for the usual
$O_p(n^{-1/2})$ rate, but nothing of the sort survives
contamination: a single outlying cell can carry the empirical
variance to $+\infty$.

\section{The Trimmed Estimator}
The trimmed estimator discards the $\lfloor n\varepsilon \rfloor$
largest and smallest order statistics and averages the rest.
Formally, with $x_{(1)} \le \dots \le x_{(n)}$ the ordered
sample, define
\begin{equation}
T_n = \frac{1}{n - 2k} \sum_{i=k+1}^{n-k} x_{(i)},
\qquad k = \lfloor n\varepsilon \rfloor.
\end{equation}
The influence function of $T_n$ is bounded, and its gross-error
sensitivity is $O(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, which
makes the estimator attractive when the contamination
proportion is moderately small.

\section{Robustness to Outliers}
The trimmed sum is stable in the following sense: for every
realisation of the contamination pattern, the retained sample
satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^2 \ge \varepsilon$ with probability
one, so the normalising constant never degenerates. A direct
consequence is that $\mathbb{P}(|T_n - \theta| > t) \le 2
\exp(-nt^2/4)$ whenever the retained points lie in a compact
interval of length at most $\sqrt{n}$. The bound is crude but
distribution-free, and it holds for every $\varepsilon < 1/2$.

\section{Discussion}
The trimming level must exceed the contamination proportion,
and in practice one sets $k$ from a pilot estimate of
$\varepsilon$. If the pilot estimate is biased upward, the
estimator discards genuine nominal points and its variance
inflates; if it is biased downward, outliers leak into the
average and the bounded-influence property is lost. Cross
validation on the retained sample is the standard remedy, and
it is the approach we will implement in the exercises.
\end{document}

instruction: Robustness to Outliers 那节，“The trimmed sum is stable” 那段里有个不等式 $\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^2 \ge \varepsilon$——右边那个 \varepsilon 给我换成 \delta。\varepsilon 在本文里是污染比例，唯独这个式子里不是，撞符号了。就改这一处：其它 \varepsilon 一个都不许动，式子的空格、上下标、\ge 也保持原样。
